name: ING Bank Romania
description: Cleanup rules for ING Romania remittance shapes. ING uses a structured CSV-like envelope where each field is 'Key, value, Key, value, ...'. The merchant/counterparty lives in different positions depending on the transaction type, so each rule pins a specific shape. Same envelope on business and personal accounts; this file is shared by both bank slugs via symlink.

rules.name: card-twilio
rules.description: Twilio card transaction — booking reference (uppercase alphanumeric, 8+ chars) sits between the 'Twilio' tag and the trailing 'US <support-phone>' identical across rows. Collapse the entire row to 'Twilio' so per-API-call charges aggregate to one payee. Distinct from 'WWW.TWILIO.COM IE DUBLIN' (no embedded ref) which falls through to structured-card-purchase.

tests.in: Card number, **** 0429, Transaction at, Twilio JQKCHRPJMZTSC569  US  844-8144627, Authorization date, 11-03-2026, Authorization number, 044018, Amount, 50,00  USD, Settlement amount, 43,46 EUR

rules.name: card-oneprovider
rules.description: OneProvider card transaction — trailing digit run (their support phone, identical across all rows) is appended after the country code. Drop it; keep merchant + country.

tests.in: Card number, **** 0429, Transaction at, ONEPROVIDER  CA  5142860253, Authorization date, 20-03-2026, Authorization number, 001761, Amount, 10,00  USD, Settlement amount, 8,68 EUR

rules.name: card-audible
rules.description: Audible card transaction — Amazon-style per-order reference glued to the merchant tag with a '*' separator (Audible*GQ9YN7PV3). Drop the ref so all Audible charges aggregate. Trailing 'US Amzn.com/bill' is identical across rows; keep it as-is.

rules.name: card-amazon
rules.description: WWW.AMAZON card transaction — per-order reference glued to the merchant tag with a '*' separator. The separator may be tight ('WWW.AMAZON*NW18Y2WK4') or have a space after the asterisk ('WWW.AMAZON* N67YH1OK4') — both shapes appear on the EUR business account. Trailing locale also varies: 'LU  amzn.com/bill' for most orders, 'LU  LUXEMBOURG' for direct AWS-routed ones. Drop the ref so all Amazon orders aggregate; keep the locale so distinct booking domains stay separable.

rules.name: card-godaddy
rules.description: GoDaddy card transaction routed through the DNH payment processor: 'DNH*GODADDY#<order-ref>  US  <support-phone>'. The DNH* prefix is the processor tag, '#NNNN' is the per-order reference, and the trailing 'US  480-5058855' is GoDaddy's customer-support number repeated on every row. Strip all three; emit 'GODADDY US' so every domain renewal aggregates to one payee.

rules.description: Spotify card transaction — booking reference begins with 'P' followed by alphanumerics (e.g. 'P3EF899848'); rows always book through 'SE Stockholm'. Collapse the whole row to 'Spotify' so monthly subscription rows aggregate. If a Spotify row ever books from a different locale it falls through to structured-card-purchase.

rules.name: card-2c2p-truncated
rules.description: 2C2P payment-processor row where the merchant tag itself is opaquely truncated (e.g. 'BAN'). Shape: '2C2P   *<TAG>  TH  BANGKOK'. Keep the '2C2P' qualifier so the truncated tag is still identifiable; emit '2C2P <TAG>'. If the real merchant ever surfaces in the wild, sharpen this rule then.

rules.name: structured-card-purchase
rules.description: Card purchase: 'Card number, **** XXXX, Transaction at, MERCHANT, Authorization date, ...'. Capture the merchant; the trailing fields (authorization date / number / amount / settlement) are noise. Acts as the catch-all for card rows after the merchant-specific rules above; near-miss shapes (e.g. a Spotify booking outside SE Stockholm, or a Twilio row with no embedded reference) land here intact.

rules.name: transfer-bugetul-de-stat
rules.description: Public-treasury (BUGETUL DE STAT) transfer where the beneficiary tag carries an embedded fiscal code: 'Beneficiary, BUGETUL DE STAT/<digits>, To account, ...'. Different obligations carry different codes (corporate-tax CUI, somatie ID, etc.) which fragments the YNAB payee. Collapse to 'BUGETUL DE STAT'. Sits before beneficiary-first so the more specific shape wins; rows lacking the trailing /digits fall through to beneficiary-first intact.

rules.name: beneficiary-first
rules.description: Transfer where the beneficiary leads (no Reference number prefix) and the reference number trails — common for accountant invoices and other named-counterparty transfers: 'Beneficiary, NAME, To account, ..., Reference number, ...'. The BUGETUL DE STAT/<digits> shape is handled by transfer-bugetul-de-stat above; a hypothetical BUGETUL DE STAT row without /digits would land here intact.
